No sound set of lemmas can make `prop` inductive for this RTL: **the bound can be violated**.

A reachable state has `count == 64`, `alloc == 0`, `free == 0`, and `nack == 0`. On the next rising edge, the input block can execute its blocking assignment `alloc = 1` before the count block runs, while the continuous assignment to `nack` has not yet updated. The count block can then evaluate `alloc & ~nack` as true and set `count` to **65**. SystemVerilog permits this ordering of active-region events, so an occupancy-count lemma would not be sound for the code as written. ([fpga.mit.edu](https://fpga.mit.edu/6205/_static/F25/documentation/1800-2017.pdf))

Use nonblocking assignments and a consistently evaluated allocation decision to remove the race; then `count == $countones(busy)` is a useful candidate invariant to prove. Also, `prop` needs a clock when it is asserted unless its assertion context supplies one. ([fpga.mit.edu](https://fpga.mit.edu/6205/_static/F25/documentation/1800-2017.pdf))

**No sound lemma set can prove `prop` for this RTL as written:** `count <= SIZE` has a legal counterexample. The two clocked blocks use blocking assignments, and events in the active region may execute in different orders. ([accellera.org](https://accellera.org/images/eda/sv-bc/att-0517/01-schedSem-svLRM-v6.pdf))

With the default parameters, fill all 64 slots, then clock `alloc_raw=0` so `alloc=0` and `nack=0`. On the next edge, set `alloc_raw=1` and `free_raw=0`. If the control block updates `alloc` before the count block runs, but `nack` has not yet updated, the count block sees `alloc=1, nack=0` and changes `count` from 64 to **65**. A lemma cannot make that reachable violation disappear. ([accellera.org](https://accellera.org/images/eda/sv-bc/att-0517/01-schedSem-svLRM-v6.pdf))

To make the intended proof possible, remove the clock-edge race—for example, use nonblocking assignments for the clocked state updates—and give `prop` an explicit `@(posedge clock)` (or provide a default clock). Then `count == $countones(busy)` is the natural occupancy invariant to prove before the bound. ([accellera.org](https://accellera.org/images/eda/sv-ec/8246.html?utm_source=openai))

<json>
{
  "lemmas": [
    {
      "lemma": "property lemma_1; @(posedge clock) (count == $countones(busy)); endproperty",
      "explanation": "The occupancy counter equals the number of busy entries. Initially, both are zero. An accepted allocation selects a previously free entry and increments both quantities. A free operation decrements both quantities only when its addressed entry was busy. When both operations occur, an occupied entry being freed differs from the previously free entry selected for allocation, so their effects remain consistent; freeing an already free entry has no effect. At full occupancy, nack prevents allocation. Thus, the equality is preserved by one transition for the supplied parameters. Since the SIZE-bit busy vector has at most SIZE set bits, this invariant directly implies count <= SIZE and makes the strengthened target 1-inductive."
    }
  ]
}
</json>
